Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

# Summary of the 2015 UK Government Manifesto

## Economic Policy

The manifesto centres on continuing an economic recovery plan initiated five years prior. Key commitments include eliminating the budget deficit through spending controls, welfare savings, and tackling tax avoidance. The plan involves reducing government spending by one percent annually in real terms, with the goal of achieving a budget surplus by 2018-19. 

Tax policies include raising the personal tax allowance to £12,500 and the higher rate threshold to £50,000, while committing to no increases in VAT, National Insurance, or Income Tax rates. The document promises to maintain competitive business taxation and conduct a major review of business rates.

## Regional Development

Significant investment is pledged for regional infrastructure, including £13 billion for northern transport links, improvements to Midlands connectivity, and enhanced links to East Anglia and the South West. The manifesto proposes devolving powers to cities with elected mayors, allowing some councils to retain 100 percent of business rates growth.

## Infrastructure and Transport

Commitments include £38 billion for rail network improvements, £15 billion for roads, and freezing commuter rail fares in real terms. Universal broadband coverage reaching 95 percent of the UK by 2017 is promised, alongside improved mobile coverage targets.

## Employment and Skills

The plan targets full employment and creating two million additional jobs. Three million new apprenticeships are pledged, alongside abolishing long-term youth unemployment through a Youth Allowance system requiring young claimants to take apprenticeships, traineeships, or community work after six months.

## Welfare Reform

Welfare policies include capping household benefits at £23,000 annually, freezing working-age benefits for two years, and completing Universal Credit rollout. The manifesto proposes reviewing support for those with treatable conditions like addiction.

## Immigration

Immigration controls include requiring EU migrants to live and contribute for four years before claiming tax credits or child benefit, ending housing benefit for EU jobseekers, and preventing child benefit claims for children living abroad. Enforcement measures include satellite tracking for foreign offenders facing deportation.

## Education

Education commitments include maintaining per-pupil funding, expanding academies and free schools, and opening 500 new free schools. Standards focus on literacy and numeracy, with resits required for those not meeting primary school standards.

## Health Service

The National Health Service receives pledges of continued real-terms spending increases, with £8 billion additional funding promised by 2020. Seven-day GP access and same-day appointments for over-75s are committed, alongside integration of health and social care services.

## Housing

Housing policies include building 200,000 starter homes at 20 percent below market price for first-time buyers under 40, extending Right to Buy to housing association tenants, and continuing Help to Buy schemes.

## Environment and Energy

Environmental commitments include creating marine protected areas, investing £3 billion in countryside enhancement, and building 1,400 flood defence schemes. Energy policy includes supporting shale gas development while ending subsidies for new onshore wind farms.

## Justice and Security

Security measures include maintaining intelligence agency funding, introducing new powers to disrupt terrorist plots, and creating banning orders for extremist organisations. The manifesto proposes replacing human rights legislation with domestic alternatives.

## Pensions

Pension policies maintain the triple lock ensuring minimum 2.5 percent annual increases. Inheritance tax changes include raising the effective threshold for couples to £1 million for family homes.

## Constitutional Matters

Constitutional changes include implementing devolution agreements for Scotland and Wales, introducing voting arrangements requiring consent from relevant territorial representatives for matters affecting only specific parts of the UK, and holding a referendum on EU membership by 2017.

## International Policy

International commitments include maintaining the nuclear deterrent, meeting NATO spending targets of two percent of national income on defence, and continuing international development spending at 0.7 percent of national income.
